strengths: Novel unifying framework for analyzing diverse perturbation sources (SGD, label, quantization, pruning) under a single TPV lens
Impressive TPV stability result (Theorem 3.1): training-set TPV converges to test-set TPV, decoupled from generalization—first such result for parameter perturbations
Striking empirical validation showing TPV stability holds even at width=1 across 5+ orders of magnitude despite theory assuming infinite width
Thorough experimental work: 324+ synthetic configurations, multiple architectures (MLP, ResNet, MobileNet, BERT), consistent patterns across datasets
Honest and detailed treatment of limitations: clearly identifies when TPV becomes uninformative, acknowledges numerical intractability of label noise computation for deep networks
Practical training-set-based model selection without test labels across four deployment scenarios
Well-executed overall: clear writing, comprehensive appendices with full proofs and experimental details
weaknesses: Significant theory-practice gap: Theorem 3.1 assumes m→∞ and isotropic perturbations, yet stability empirically holds at width=1 with structured perturbations; bound may be loose and doesn't explain why overparameterization isn't necessary

Label noise TPV for deep networks is numerically intractable (condition numbers 10^6-10^8); proposed perturb-and-retrain heuristic (D.3.4) doesn't achieve exact min-norm solutions and involves many hyperparameters with unclear sensitivity
Limited novelty in components: Tr(H_eff C) from prior work; label noise analysis under linearization standard; main contribution is unification rather than new analytical tools

TPV-generalization correlation is regime-dependent and fragile: U-shaped with opposite trends in high vs low training loss regimes; cross-architecture model selection (Figure 25) shows weaker or inconsistent trends
Applications are incremental: JBR pruning closely resembles existing Jacobian Criterion with only modest improvements; model selection unreliable across architectures

Restrictive assumptions limit scope: isotropic covariance excludes structured perturbations; first-order approximation breaks for larger perturbations (σ=0.1); minimum-norm assumption may not hold in practice
Insufficient exploration of hyperparameter sensitivity in label noise TPV algorithm and limited ablation studies on design choices
